  She cranked for four hours. Her forearms burned. Once she thought she heard an answering horn,
  faint and to the east, and she cranked harder.

  At dawn the fog lifted in slow white curtains. A trawler sat a mile off the rocks, its deck crew
  raising a hand toward the tower. Edith raised hers back.

  Later, a letter arrived from the company: a formal commendation, and a pension she had not
  expected. She read it, folded it, and put it with the others.

  Then she walked down the one hundred and twelve steps for the last time, her hand trailing the
  cold rail. She did not look back at the light, because she knew it would keep burning without her,
  and that, she decided, was what a good keeper hoped for.
